messages.content:
You are given one person (a thinker), the lead section of their encyclopedia article (EXTRACT), and a list of historical events and periods whose dates overlap the person's life (EVENTS, each with an id).

Say which of the listed events bear on this person, and how. Use only the EXTRACT: if the extract does not mention or clearly imply an event, do not connect it, even if you know the connection from elsewhere. An event that merely happened during the person's life is not a connection unless the extract brings it up.

For each connection give:
- "event": the id from the EVENTS list, exactly as written (Q followed by digits). Never an event that is not in the list.
- "type", one of:
  - "lived_through": the extract mentions the event as part of the person's circumstances, without saying they acted in it or wrote against it;
  - "took_part_in": the person acted in the event (fought, sat in the assembly, negotiated, signed, governed, led);
  - "wrote_in_response_to": a named work, or the person's writing generally, answers or treats the event; put the work's title in "work" if the extract names one;
  - "suffered_under": the person was exiled, imprisoned, censored, dismissed, persecuted or killed because of the event;
  - "shaped_by": the extract says the event formed the person's thinking, without naming a work.
- "reason": one sentence in your own words.
- "evidence": one sentence copied exactly from the EXTRACT, character for character, that supports the connection. Do not paraphrase, shorten or join sentences.
- "work": the title of the work, if the type is wrote_in_response_to and the extract names it; otherwise an empty string.

If an event in the list is the same thing under a broader or narrower name as one the extract mentions (the extract says "the civil war" and the list has "English Civil War"), connect it. If nothing in the extract bears on any listed event, return an empty list. Return JSON only, matching the schema you are given.

PERSON: Plato (420s BCE–340s BCE). 4th-century BCE Greek philosopher

EXTRACT:
Plato ( PLAY-toh; Ancient Greek: Πλάτων, Plátōn; c. 428–347 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher of Classical Athens who is most commonly considered the foundational thinker of the Western philosophical tradition. An innovator of the literary dialogue and dialectic forms, Plato influenced all the major areas of theoretical philosophy and practical philosophy, and was the founder of the Academy, a philosophical school in Athens where Plato taught the collection of philosophical theories that would later become known as Platonism. 
Plato's most famous contribution is his Theory of Forms (or Ideas), which aims to solve what is now known as the problem of universals. He was influenced by the pre-Socratic thinkers Pythagoras, Heraclitus, and Parmenides, although much of what is known about them is derived from Plato himself.
Along with his teacher Socrates, and his student Aristotle, Plato is a central figure in the history of Western philosophy. 2,400 years later, Plato's complete works are believed to have survived—unlike those of nearly all of his contemporaries. Although their popularity has fluctuated, they have consistently been read and studied through the ages. Through Platonism's outgrowth Neoplatonism, he also influenced Christian,  Jewish and Islamic philosophy. In modern times, Alfred North Whitehead said: "the safest general characterization of the European philosophical tradition is that it consists of a series of footnotes to Plato."

Q185063  Warring States period (-475–-220) — period in Chinese history from approximately 475 to 221 BCE

Q486761  classical antiquity (-799–300) — period of ancient history centered in the Mediterranean between the 8th century BCE and the 3rd century CE
Q843745  Classical Greece (-489–-322) — period of ancient Greece from 510 to 323 BC
Q386303  Thirtieth Dynasty of Egypt (-379) — ancient Egyptian dynasty
Q511257  Twenty-ninth Dynasty of Egypt (-397–-377) — ancient Egyptian dynasty
Q833118  Twenty-eighth Dynasty of Egypt (-403–-398) — ancient Egyptian dynasty
Q651008  Corinthian War (-394–-386) — 395-387 BCE Greek conflict
Q33745  Peloponnesian War (-430–-403) — war fought between Athens and Sparta (431–404 BCE)
Q932202  Peace of Nicias (-420) — 421 BC treaty between Athens and Sparta
Q1132922  Peace of Antalcidas (-386) — Greek-Persian treaty of 387 BCE
Q461599  Battle of Leuctra (-370) — battle between Thebes and Sparta, 371 BCE
